wstep: This card describes how NCHFP freezes strawberries: whole in syrup, or whole, sliced or crushed with sugar.

akapity: Choose fully ripe, firm berries with a deep red color and discard immature and defective fruit.
Wash the strawberries and remove the caps.
NCHFP uses US measures: a cup holds about 237 ml.
Add 3/4 cup of sugar to 1 quart (1 1/3 pounds) of strawberries and mix thoroughly.
Stir until most of the sugar has dissolved, or let stand for 15 minutes.
Sliced or crushed strawberries use the same amount of sugar.
Put whole berries into containers and cover them with cold 50% syrup.
For 50% syrup, dissolve 4 cups of sugar in 4 cups of lukewarm water until the solution is clear; this makes about 6 cups, and the syrup must be chilled before use.
Use just enough cold syrup to cover the fruit, about 1/2–2/3 cup per pint.
To keep the fruit under the syrup, place a small piece of crumpled parchment paper on top and press the fruit down before sealing.

Leave headspace: in wide-mouth containers 1/2 inch (about 1.3 cm) for a pint and 1 inch (about 2.5 cm) for a quart, in narrow-mouth containers 3/4 inch (about 1.9 cm) for a pint and 1 1/2 inches (about 3.8 cm) for a quart.
Frozen food is safe as long as it stays frozen; once it thaws above 40 °F (about 4 °C), bacteria present before freezing can begin to multiply.
